critical.scanSeverityFrom: CISA-ADP CVSS 3.1 9.8; the curl project publishes no CVSS
critical.upstreamSeverity: curl.se: Low; libcurl only, not the command-line tool
critical.knownExploited: No KEV entry; CISA SSVC exploitation poc, automatable yes (record of 2026-07-06)
critical.needs: CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS or CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E, then curl_easy_reset and curl_easy_cleanup
critical.exposure: Not reachable: nothing in the image sets HTTP/2 stream dependencies, and the application makes no libcurl request at this revision

accepted.rationale: A use-after-free at a handle's cleanup, needing HTTP/2 stream dependencies that the curl project calls extremely rarely used.
accepted.mitigation: The application calls neither libcurl nor its HTTP client; the only curl in use is the health check's fixed loopback request.
accepted.reviewTrigger: TASK-013 before its HTTP or S3 integration: check that its client sets no stream dependency.

accepted.debianStatus: trixie vulnerable, <no-dsa> (Minor issue); fixed in unstable 2.14.5; no trixie-backports package

critical.scanSeverityFrom: NVD's primary CVSS 3.1 9.8, Critical; the CNA (Canonical) gives CVSS 4.0 7.0, High
critical.upstreamSeverity: Canonical, as CNA: High, attack complexity High
critical.knownExploited: No KEV entry; CISA SSVC exploitation none, automatable no (record of 2026-06-22); the CNA's vector states E:P, a proof of concept
critical.needs: PHP parsing attacker-supplied XML with faulty entity resolution in its internal subset, through the XML parser
critical.exposure: Not reachable: no route accepts XML; images go through GD, which does not use libxml2. The one call that parses is Termwind's DOMDocument::loadHTML of the framework's console components, at each container start, in schedule:run, in the migration job and in the framework's operator commands, on fixed framework text with its content escaped: the HTML parser, whose doctype code does not call xmlParseInternalSubset (HTMLparser.c of 2.9.14). Other vendor parsers run on no input from a request

accepted.rationale: A use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset; the remote denial of service needs the XML parser run on crafted XML.
accepted.mitigation: No XML input exists in any route, command or upload; SVG and other XML formats are refused by the media pipeline. Console components print fixed framework text and the schedule's identifiers, and the application's own commands print through $this->info, $this->error and $this->line, which do not use Termwind.
accepted.reviewTrigger: Any Task that accepts or parses XML, an XML-based file format or an import through libxml2, or prints request-derived or stored text through a console component.

accepted.debianStatus: trixie vulnerable, with no note of Debian's assessment; unfixed in unstable 2.43-7 as well (Debian bug 1152640, GLIBC-SA-2026-0025)
accepted.rationale: gettext accepts a LANGUAGE entry holding a slash or equal to .., so a crafted .mo file can be loaded from another path; it needs the environment set across a trust boundary and that file in place.

accepted.reviewTrigger: Debian's assessment or a fix; an SSH server or the gettext extension added to the image; a program started with an environment built from input; gate RELEASE.

accepted.debianStatus: Not read from Debian's tracker by this run (CE-47); Grype's database of 2026-11-06T06:21:59Z, built from it, gives the state not-fixed and no fixed version for Debian 13, and the build of the same run, which upgrades every package from trixie, trixie-updates and trixie-security, left zlib1g at this version: no supported fix exists in Debian 13
accepted.rationale: A flaw in gz_write, the core of zlib's gzip-file writer (gzwrite, gzfwrite, gzputs, gzputc), High by the scan's database, which records no known exploitation (EPSS 0.00592); a public proof of concept is taken to exist (D-123). Its description was not reachable by this run; the assessment holds for any flaw of that writer, because its code runs only when a program writes a gzip file through it.
accepted.mitigation: Nothing in the image writes through zlib's gzip-file writer. PHP reaches it only through gzopen, gzwrite, gzputs or the compress.zlib:// wrapper, which nothing in app/, config/, routes/, bootstrap/, database/, the views or any production dependency calls; Guzzle only inflates response bodies. pg_dump --format=custom compresses with deflate() and writes its archive with plain file writes, and pg_restore --list only reads it; age is Go without cgo. GD's libpng, Nginx (no gzip directive), libcurl, OpenSSL and GnuTLS use deflate() and inflate() alone; apt and dpkg-deb write gzip files only in root package operations, which no process of the running image performs.
accepted.reviewTrigger: A fix in Debian 13, which the build installs and the gate then prints as ACCEPTED_NOT_REPORTED, or known exploitation, which the gate then refuses; any write through zlib's gzip-file writer: PHP's gzopen, gzwrite, gzputs or compress.zlib://, pg_dump's plain or directory format with compression, or a program that writes gzip files through zlib; a description of the CVE that names a path outside that writer; a change of the base image or of PHP's build; gate RELEASE.
